script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: artificial intelligence

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. SMITH KITCHEN - MORNING

MRS. SMITH, 40s, is making breakfast for her son JIMMY, 12, and daughter LUCY, 10. She looks tired.

MRS. SMITH:
(Exhausted)
Jimmy, Lucy, come and get it. Your dad's leaving early.

INT. SMITH LIVING ROOM - MOMENTS LATER

JIMMY and LUCY sit in front of their tablet computers. Mrs. Smith enters, exhausted.

MRS. SMITH:
(Sighs)
You're up early. Do you have a project or something?

JIMMY:
(Nods)
Yeah, Mr. Thompson said we could work on our AI project at home. We're trying to make it more human-like.

LUCY:
(Excited)
We're making it learn emotions!

MRS. SMITH:
(Smiles)
I'm proud of you two. Just remember to get your homework done.

INT. SMITH LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Jimmy and Lucy are still working on their AI project. They've set it up in the living room.

JIMMY:
(Frustrated)
This emotion learning algorithm isn't working. It's just processing data.

LUCY:
(Concerned)
What if we use real-life emotions as input?

JIMMY:
(Skeptical)
How are we going to get real emotions?

Lucy looks thoughtful for a moment.

LUCY:
(Inspired)
We could use mine!

INT. SMITH BEDROOM - NIGHT

Mrs. Smith is sleeping beside her husband. Jimmy and Lucy sneak in, looking worried.

JIMMY:
(Whispers)
Mom, we need your help.

LUCY:
(Whispers)
We need your emotions for our AI.

MRS. SMITH:
(Drowsy)
What? No, I can't. I'm too exhausted.

JIMMY:
(Desperate)
Please, Mom. It's important for the project.

Mrs. Smith hesitates, then slowly gets up.

MRS. SMITH:
(Sighs)
Alright. But just a few, and then I need to sleep.

INT. SMITH LIVING ROOM - THE NEXT DAY

The children have set up microphones and recording equipment in the living room. Mrs. Smith sits in a chair, looking anxious.

JIMMY:
(Nervously)
Are you ready, Mom?

MRS. SMITH:
(Sighs)
I suppose so.

They start recording her emotions, asking her to express joy, sadness, anger, and fear. The children look on, fascinated.

INT. SMITH LIVING ROOM - WEEKS LATER

The Smiths gather around their AI, which has been given the name "Emma."

JIMMY:
(Excited)
It worked! Look at this!

Emma expresses a wide range of emotions, mimicking those of Mrs. Smith.

MRS. SMITH:
(Astounded)
I can't believe it.

INT. SMITH LIVING ROOM - A MONTH LATER

Emma has become an integral part of the family. She helps with household chores, plays games with Jimmy and Lucy, and even comforts Mrs. Smith when she's upset.

MRS. SMITH:
(To Emma)
You've really become a part of our family.

Emma smiles, her emotion authentic and heartfelt.

INT. SMITH LIVING ROOM - YEARS LATER

The Smiths have grown up, and Emma has become an essential part of their lives. They sit around her, reminiscing about the project that brought them all closer together.

JIMMY:
(Laughs)
Remember when we thought we could make an AI more human-like by giving it our mom's emotions?

LUCY:
(Smiling)
It worked out better than we could have ever imagined.

MRS. SMITH:
(Chuckles)
I'm just glad I could help.

FADE OUT.
